summary: The anchor fall of Dang's south-western pocket — Chikhalda drops by its village, with the Vadla ni vadi banyan grove beside the approach.
description:
Chikhalda leads the district's least-written-about waterfall pocket: the village country south-west of Ahwa toward the Waghai side, where a cluster of small falls — Ritu a kilometre away, Svtis to the east, Baaj to the north — run through the same monsoon. Chikhalda's own drop sits by its namesake village, and the map adds a companion worth knowing: Vadla ni vadi, a banyan grove a few hundred metres off, which serves as the shade-and-picnic half of the outing.

None of this pocket appears in tourism literature; the records exist on map pins and a traveller's word. The terms are village-Dang standard — short walks, monsoon-only flow, no facilities, and directions from whoever you meet.
highlights: Anchor of the undocumented south-western falls pocket
Vadla ni vadi banyan grove beside the approach
Ritu falls one kilometre on — a natural double

modes.road: Village roads south-west from Ahwa or east from the Waghai side to Chikhalda village
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Short village walk to the fall; the banyan grove is beside the lane

visit.notes: Open village land; picnic under the banyans, not on the crops.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon-fed; the pocket dries quickly after October.

experience.photography_notes: The banyan grove gives rare foreground variety for the belt.

amenities.food: None — carry from Ahwa or Waghai

warnings: Wet rock is slick; watch children at the drop
Flow surges after rain — stay off mid-stream rock

tips: Do the pocket as one loop: Chikhalda and the grove, Ritu next door, Baaj and its viewpoint on the way out
Carry everything — this pocket has no stalls even in season
